title: Discovery of diverse GPCR-targeted antibodies using integrated technologies
body_text: Blackler R, et al. Antibody Engineering & Therapeutics US, December 2023 This poster describes the identification of antibodies against an established GPCR target, chemokine receptor 8 (CCR8). Hundreds of diverse antibodies were discovered using protein- and DNA-based immunizations coupled with microfluidic single-cell screening. High-throughput function-based screening was used to down-select antibodies based on ADCC reporter activity. Antibodies were optimized for developability using structure-guided protein engineering technologies paired with high-throughput antibody assessment. Selected antibodies show strong ADCC reporter activity similar to a clinical benchmark and favorable developability properties. ‍

title: Key Differences Between Centralized and Distributed Control Systems in Vehicle Design
summary: Learn about the key differences between centralized and distributed systems in vehicle designs and some key consideration
body_text: Distributed CAN modules reduce downtime in mobile equipment systems by eliminating single points of failure, enabling fault isolation, and improving overall system reliability. The difference between centralized and distributed control systems in vehicle design are how they control power and manage operations across multiple modules. This provides faster response time, greater efficiency and enhanced fault tolerance. We will dive deeper into each contrast and when to implement them into your next project. Key Difference The main differences between the two architectures determine everything from a vehicle’s safety and overall functions. Wiring Complexity and Weight Centralized: This requires wire across the entire system to connect all sensors and actuators to the central hub. The heavy wiring harness reduces fuel efficiency and range. Distributed: Localized modules connected to devices will communicate back to the main system like a data bus, while reducing weight. Tolerance and Safety Centralized: Operates with a single point of failure Distributed: Highly fault-tolerant for any localized controller fails, while the rest of the vehicle remains completely operational. Power and Scalability Centralized: Scales well for software updates and processing massive data. Distributed: Processing burdens are shared. Response Time Centralized: Slower for micro-second Distributed: Higher response time for real-time applications. Key Design Considerations CAN J1939 Communication offers high-speed communication for faster execution of vital processes and faster analysis of microprocessor unit messages, especially in large vehicles used in transportation, agriculture and industrial settings. Modular architecture supports specialized hardware modules that communicate via CAN bus and provides easier system scaling. Diagnostic Proper architecture ensures healthy system health and performance. Summary of Suitability Depending on the specific use of vehicle design, both centralize and decentralized control modules provides their own power system reliability.

body_text: Finding the right people is harder than it looks. Job boards overflow with applications, hiring managers drown in resumes, and strong candidates often accept offers elsewhere before a second interview is even scheduled. Recruitment Automation Tools have reshaped how companies approach this challenge, helping teams move faster, reduce bias, and focus energy on the candidates most likely to succeed. A smarter hiring process does not stop at the offer letter. Onboarding, role clarity, and early engagement all determine whether a new hire stays long enough to make a real contribution. Companies that treat recruitment and retention as a connected system, rather than separate problems, consistently build stronger teams, and that starts with a reliable global HR system . At the same time, 63% of employers identify skills gaps as the biggest barrier to business transformation, and nearly 40% of skills required for today's roles are expected to change by 2030. Reactive hiring, where recruitment begins only when a seat becomes vacant, cannot keep pace with that rate of change. Candidate experience has become a measurable competitive factor. Up to 80% of applicants abandon applications because of lengthy or unclear processes, and 64% of HR professionals say finding qualified talent has become harder even as applicant volumes grow. More applications do not automatically mean better fits, and organizations still optimizing for volume rather than match quality are losing candidates who have real options elsewhere. Skills-based hiring is gaining traction as a more reliable signal of a candidate's capabilities than credentials or linear career history. LinkedIn's Future of Recruiting 2025 report found that 93% of talent acquisition professionals believe accurately assessing candidate skills is essential to improving hire quality, and organizations conducting the most skills-based searches are 12% more likely to make a quality hire. This approach also reduces unconscious bias by tying evaluation criteria to demonstrated ability rather than background markers. Slow hiring timelines carry a direct competitive cost. It takes an average of 44 days to hire a new employee according to Cisive's 2025 hiring challenges report, and a bad hire can cost up to 30% of that employee's first-year earnings. In fast-moving talent markets, process delays are not a neutral operational fact; they are a signal to candidates about how an organization functions. Regional hiring in MENA adds layers of complexity that a single unified strategy rarely accounts for. In the UAE and Saudi Arabia, Emiratisation and Saudisation programs carry real financial consequences for organizations that miss targets, and both countries have enacted Personal Data Protection Laws that govern how candidate information is collected and stored during recruitment. LinkedIn's Future of Recruiting 2025 MENA report also found that 62% of recruiters in the region report difficulty finding qualified candidates, making process speed and clarity more important, not less. Recruitment data fragmented across disconnected tools makes it nearly impossible to improve hiring quality over time. Without visibility into which sourcing channels produce candidates who pass interviews and stay beyond their first year, investment gets allocated by habit rather than evidence. Cercli's global HR system addresses this by consolidating recruitment, onboarding, payroll, and analytics into a single, connected platform, so that candidate information flows automatically and hiring teams can make decisions based on data. Why Corporate Recruitment Strategies Need to Evolve Corporate recruitment has changed dramatically . The talent market is shaped by ongoing skills shortages , rising candidate expectations , and rapid change . According to HR Lineup's Recruitment Statistics Every HR Should Know in 2025 , 76% of employers report talent shortages at an all-time high , pushing businesses to expand hiring beyond traditional borders . " 76% of employers report talent shortages at an all-time high, pushing businesses to expand hiring beyond traditional borders." — HR Lineup, 2025 🚨 Warning: Companies that fail to evolve their recruitment strategies risk falling behind in an increasingly competitive talent landscape . The shortage is not a temporary trend. 🔑 Takeaway: A 76% talent shortage rate signals that traditional hiring approaches are insufficient. Businesses must rethink their recruitment models to stay competitive and attract top-tier candidates in a shrinking talent pool. Why is the hiring process itself the biggest failure point? The failure point is usually the process itself, not the pipeline. Today, 63% of employers say skills gaps are the biggest barrier to business transformation, according to the World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025 , and nearly 40% of the skills required for today's roles are expected to change by 2030. Reactive hiring cannot keep pace with this change. Candidate expectations have shifted sharply. Job seekers now evaluate employers by researching culture, assessing values, and forming opinions before applying. Research from LinkedIn's 2025 talent report found that 64% of HR professionals say finding qualified talent has become harder, even as applicant volumes grow. The result: more applications, fewer fits . How do complex processes cause qualified candidates to disappear? Most teams respond by adding steps: more screening rounds, longer job descriptions, extra approvals. LinkedIn's research on candidate drop-off shows that up to 80% of applicants abandon applications due to lengthy or unclear processes. A global HR system like Cercli consolidates hiring workflows, candidate management, and onboarding into a single connected platform, eliminating gaps where qualified candidates can disappear between stages. What separates organizations that consistently win at talent acquisition? The organizations winning at talent acquisition treat recruitment as a continuous business function rather than a reactive response to open headcount. According to LinkedIn's Future of Recruiting 2025 report , 93% of talent acquisition professionals believe that accurately assessing candidate skills is essential to improving hire quality, and organizations that conduct the most skills-based searches are 12% more likely to make a quality hire. Recruitment strategy and business strategy are no longer separate conversations. Workforce planning, employer branding, skills-based hiring, and recruitment analytics all feed into the same outcome: building a team capable of delivering on business needs. Winning organizations build talent pipelines before they need them, use data to understand what drives successful hires, and invest in candidate experience as seriously as customer experience. Knowing your strategy needs to evolve is only half the answer. The harder question is which specific approaches move the needle. Related Reading Candidate Screening Questions Candidate Screening Process Automated Candidate Screening Steps in the Recruitment Process End to End Recruitment Process Recruiting Funnel Metrics AI in Recruitment Examples Recruitment Lifecycle Best Recruitment Strategies 12 Corporate Recruitment Strategies That Deliver Better Hiring Results A good corporate recruitment strategy is a connected system where employer branding , talent pipeline development , structured interviewing , and data-driven decision-making support each other. When one part is weak , the whole system slows down . "A corporate recruitment strategy is only as strong as its weakest link — every component from branding to structured interviewing must work in harmony to deliver better hiring results ." Strong recruitment systems depend on optimizing each core component: Employer branding – Attracts top talent organically; weak branding results in fewer qualified applicants. Talent pipeline development – Builds a ready pool of candidates; weak pipelines lead to slower time-to-hire. Structured interviewing – Ensures consistent candidate evaluation; poor structure creates biased or inconsistent decisions. Data-driven decision-making – Improves hiring outcomes; lack of data leads to missed opportunities for improvement. 💡 Tip: Treat your recruitment strategy as an ecosystem , not a checklist — every element must be actively maintained to keep the system performing at its peak. ⚠️ Warning: Neglecting even one pillar of your recruitment strategy can create a ripple effect that slows down the entire hiring process and costs your organization top-tier candidates . 1. Build a Strong Employer Brand Most candidates form opinions about your organization before recruiters contact them, based on reviews, LinkedIn, and employee testimonials. According to the iCIMS Blog , companies with strong employer brands see 50% more qualified applicants, so brand perception directly shapes the quality of the applicant pool. Employer branding requires consistent, specific content: real employee stories, honest descriptions of career progression, and authentic leadership voices. Authenticity filters for candidates who genuinely fit while repelling poor matches. 2. Develop Talent Pipelines Before Vacancies Open Most organizations begin recruiting when a job opening appears, starting from scratch, incurring higher costs and longer time-to-fill windows . Building talent pipelines before you need them transforms recruitment from a reactive scramble into a predictable, manageable process. Effective pipeline development means staying in contact with passive candidates through recruitment marketing, maintaining talent communities, and treating previous applicants as long-term assets. When a role opens, you reach out to people who already know your organization and have expressed interest. 3. Use Employee Referral Programs The best hires often come through people already inside the organization. CPS HR Consulting reports that employee referrals account for 30-40% of all hires at many organizations because employees understand the culture, pace, and expectations better than any job description can convey. A referral program only works if it's easy to use and consistently reinforced. Complicated submission processes, unclear reward structures , or poor communication after a referral will kill participation. The mechanics matter as much as the incentive. 4. Invest in Recruitment CRM and Candidate Relationship Management A recruitment CRM stores candidate profiles, tracks interactions, and organizes talent pools so recruiters can re-engage strong fits who weren't ready to move when first contacted. This builds talent acquisition over time rather than treating each hiring cycle as a fresh start. Spreadsheets and basic ATS notes create gaps as candidate volumes grow: follow-ups get missed, warm candidates go cold, and sourcing work repeats quarterly. Platforms like Cercli integrate recruitment, HR, and workforce management into a single platform, preventing candidate relationships from falling through the cracks between disconnected tools. 5. Combine AI With Human Decision-Making AI handles volume well: screening applications , flagging candidates who meet core criteria, summarising profiles, and scheduling interviews. This frees recruiters for work requiring human judgment—assessing cultural alignment, reading communication style, and evaluating whether someone's potential fits the team's direction. AI should reduce friction and improve consistency, not replace the professional instincts that make hiring decisions defensible. Organizations that use AI as a filter while keeping humans in the decision seat move faster without sacrificing quality. 6. Strengthen Your Careers Site and Application Experience A slow, unclear, or mobile-unfriendly careers site immediately loses qualified candidates. Your application experience reflects how your organization works: a clunky process suggests internal friction, while a clean, fast one suggests respect for candidates' time. Focus on specific improvements: clear job descriptions with realistic expectations, a mobile-optimized application form, and acknowledgment emails sent within minutes of submission each reduce drop-off at different stages. Measure candidate conversion rate as a metric, not an assumed outcome. 7. Expand Sourcing Across Multiple Channels Using only job boards reaches only active candidates already looking for work. Passive candidates, often the best performers, require different approaches: LinkedIn outreach, industry communities, university partnerships, and internal mobility programs. Evaluate channels by quality of hires , not application volume. A channel driving 40% of applications but only 5% of successful hires wastes budget. 8. Use Skills-Based Hiring Where Appropriate Many organizations are finding that degree requirements and linear career paths poorly measure actual ability. Skills-based hiring uses practical tests, technical exercises, and structured interviews to evaluate what candidates can do, rather than relying on credentials as shortcuts. This approach expands the talent pool and identifies candidates with transferable skills who would otherwise be filtered out early. The shift also reduces unconscious bias in screening. When evaluation criteria are based on demonstrated skills rather than background markers, hiring decisions become more consistent and defensible. 9. Improve Collaboration Between Recruiters and Hiring Managers Recruitment slows when recruiters and hiring managers operate from different understandings of job requirements. Before candidate searches begin, both groups must align on key skills, disqualifying factors, interview processes, and timelines. This alignment meeting prevents weeks of mismatched candidate lists and circular feedback. When both sides can see where candidates are in the process, everyone stays accountable for their part. Hiring managers can track candidate movement through each stage, recruiters can access feedback immediately, and decisions are made faster, with fewer good candidates lost to delays. 10. Prioritize Candidate Experience Throughout the Hiring Process Every touchpoint in your hiring process communicates something about your organization. A week of silence after an interview, a generic rejection email, or a scheduling process that requires five back-and-forth messages all leave impressions that candidates carry forward. Employer reputation is built one candidate interaction at a time. Even rejected candidates can become advocates or future applicants if the experience was respectful and clear. Acceptance rates, candidate satisfaction scores, and time-to-respond metrics reflect the quality of experience you're delivering, not process speed alone. 11. Measure Recruitment Performance With Meaningful Metrics Most recruitment reporting fails by focusing on volume metrics while ignoring quality indicators. Time to hire and cost per hire matter, but quality of hire, offer acceptance rate , and hiring manager satisfaction reveal whether the process produces business results. Regular reporting against these metrics identifies where the process breaks down. If qualified applicant rates are high but offer acceptance is low, the problem lies in later stages, not sourcing. Metrics make bottlenecks visible, enabling fixes. 12. Continuously Optimize Your Recruitment Strategy After any major hiring cycle, review source-of-hire data, candidate drop-off points, and hiring manager feedback. These patterns reveal improvement opportunities invisible during the hiring process itself. How do you keep your recruitment strategy current over time? Job markets change, candidate preferences shift, and new tools open up new possibilities. A hiring plan that worked well eighteen months ago might now be slower, more costly, or less effective. Building regular check-ins into your hiring operations keeps the plan current without requiring a complete overhaul. But knowing which strategies work is only part of the picture. The obstacles that stop even well-designed approaches from delivering are often the ones nobody warns you about. Common Challenges That Prevent Corporate Recruitment Success The problems nobody warns you about are rarely dramatic. They are quiet, structural, and expensive . "The most dangerous hiring obstacles aren't loud failures — they're silent inefficiencies baked into the process itself." ⚠️ Warning: If your recruitment process was never designed to scale, growth will expose every crack . The most persistent hiring failures come from processes never designed to grow , tools that don't work together , and decisions made too late . According to SHRM's 2025 Talent Trends report , 75% of HR professionals report difficulty recruiting for full-time positions , even in markets with high candidate volumes . The problem is not supply. The problem is friction . Recruitment challenges often stem from operational gaps that limit growth: Processes not built to scale – Create bottlenecks that increase as hiring volume grows. Disconnected tools – Cause data gaps, slower decisions, and fragmented workflows. Late-stage decision-making – Leads to lost candidates and higher cost-per-hire. 🔑 Takeaway: When 75% of HR professionals struggle to fill roles despite abundant candidates, the bottleneck isn't the talent market — it's the internal recruitment infrastructure . 💡 Tip: Audit your hiring workflow for friction points before investing in sourcing — more candidates won't solve a broken process . Where the process breaks before it should The failure point is invisible until it costs you someone good. A qualified candidate moves through two interview stages, then waits five days for feedback while a hiring manager juggles competing priorities. By the time the internal conversation happens, that candidate has accepted an offer elsewhere. The Cisive 2025 hiring challenges report found it takes an average of 44 days to hire a new employee—a competitive liability in fast-moving talent markets. Speed signals how your organization operates. Most recruitment teams respond by adding more touchpoints: more check-ins, more approval layers, more coordination emails. The result is delay stacked on delay. As hiring scales across departments or geographies, manual coordination loops compound. Candidate records live in one system, interview notes in another, offer approvals in someone's inbox. Platforms like Cercli consolidate hiring, HR management, and payroll into a single connected workflow, enabling recruiters to spend less time chasing information across tools and more time moving candidates forward. Why does poor measurement quietly distort recruitment strategy? The critical difference between recruitment teams that improve and those that stagnate is whether they can see what is working. Application volume tells you almost nothing about hiring quality. What matters is which sourcing channels produce candidates who pass interviews, accept offers, and stay beyond their first year. Without that visibility, recruitment investment gets allocated by habit rather than evidence, and underperforming channels get funded quarter after quarter. How does fragmented data cause workforce planning to fail? This connects directly to how workforce planning fails. When recruitment data sits fragmented across separate systems, forecasting future hiring needs becomes guesswork. Talent acquisition teams cannot identify where bottlenecks form, which roles consistently take the longest to fill, or where candidate drop-off happens most often in the funnel. The result is a recruitment strategy that responds to vacancies rather than anticipating them. A bad hire can cost a company up to 30% of the employee's first-year earnings, according to Cisive , making poor visibility costly. What works in one market does not always translate when you start hiring across borders , and the gap between strategy and execution widens in ways most recruitment playbooks never anticipate. Corporate Recruitment Considerations for Employers in MENA Hiring across MENA requires navigating distinct challenges in each country's labor law , localization policy , and workforce expectations . Success depends on treating the region as separate markets rather than a single block . "The MENA region is not a monolith — each country carries its own labour framework, nationalization quota, and cultural hiring norm that employers must understand before entering the market." — Regional HR Best Practice Insight 🎯 Key Point: MENA recruitment is never one-size-fits-all. Every market — from the UAE to Saudi Arabia to Egypt — demands a tailored compliance and hiring strategy . ⚠️ Warning: Treating MENA as a single unified market is one of the most costly mistakes a corporate employer can make — leading to compliance failures , localization penalties , and high turnover rates . Consideration Why It Matters Labour Law Variations Each country has unique contract, termination, and benefits rules Localization Policies Quotas like Saudization or Emiratization affect hiring ratios Workforce Expectations Cultural norms shape how candidates evaluate offers and employers What localization requirements actually demand The Emiratisation and Saudisation programs are structural commitments that reshape how organizations build their talent pipelines. In the UAE, private-sector companies with 50+ employees face annual Emiratisation targets, with financial penalties for failing to meet them. In Saudi Arabia, Nitaqat classifications vary by industry, company size, and occupation, so a hiring strategy that worked last year may fall short this year. Organizations treating localization as an afterthought during recruitment scramble during audit periods, an expensive mistake. How do organizations build a pipeline of qualified local talent? Building a pipeline of qualified local talent requires developing graduate programs, partnering with universities, and creating career pathways that attract Emirati and Saudi nationals before vacancies open. According to the LinkedIn Future of Recruiting 2025 MENA report , 73% of talent professionals in MENA say employer brand significantly impacts hiring. Organizations that win local talent invest in their reputation long before the job description is written. How can teams manage cross-border hiring across multiple MENA jurisdictions? Most teams manage cross-border hiring using spreadsheets, local HR contacts, and country-specific payroll tools assembled over time. This works for one or two countries, but managing employees, contractors, and Employer of Record arrangements across five or six MENA jurisdictions reveals significant problems. Cercli solves this complexity by giving recruitment and HR teams a single platform to hire, onboard, and run payroll across multiple countries without rebuilding workflows for each market. Where data privacy becomes a hiring risk Protecting candidate data is one of the biggest compliance risks organizations miss in regional recruitment. Both the UAE and Saudi Arabia have passed Personal Data Protection Laws that control how personal information is collected, stored, and shared during the hiring process. Collecting more candidate information than the job requires, or working with third-party recruitment providers that do not comply with local privacy standards, creates a risk that most organizations discover only after a breach occurs. Best practice: collect what you need, inform candidates how their data will be used, and apply consistent retention and deletion policies across all recruitment channels. Why does a slow hiring process cost you qualified candidates? LinkedIn's Future of Recruiting 2025 MENA report finds that 62% of recruiters in MENA struggle to find qualified candidates. In tight talent markets, a slow or unclear hiring process causes candidates with competing offers to accept positions elsewhere. Organizations that move quickly and communicate clearly throughout the process fill roles that competitors cannot. Speed without structure creates its own problems, which the next section addresses. body_text: Being familiar with how fiber optic systems work means getting back to the fundamentals so you can make smarter technology decisions. But I’ve noticed that questions about the basics come up often, no matter how experienced someone is. When I joined Belden a few years ago after working in the power distribution industry, I quickly realized that even seasoned professionals can benefit from clear, straightforward answers to foundational fiber questions. That’s why I put together these insights, based on presentations I often give to industry professionals to make it easier to understand what fiber really is. How are fiber optic systems different from copper? While copper cables transmit data using electrical signals, fiber uses light. By transmitting data as pulses of light rather than electrical currents, fiber optic cables eliminate many of the limitations associated with copper cables, such as excessive heat generation, concern about bundle sizes, signal degradation over distance and susceptibility to electromagnetic interference. These limitations can become issues in certain high-speed, high-density environments. But fiber is designed to overcome them. Because it transmits data as pulses of light (and at the speed of light), it can carry more information much faster and over longer distances. And because it’s immune to electromagnetic interference and uses glass instead of metal, it offers minimal signal loss. Signals remain strong and clear. One important consideration to note, however, is that fiber has its tradeoffs, just like any technology: It can’t transmit power like copper cables can. Today, it can only transmit data. How do fiber optic systems work? A fiber optic cable sends pulses of light (data) through thin strands of glass “fibers.” The heart of a fiber is its glass core, which sits in the middle of the cable, giving light a path to travel down the cable to a receiving device. Data travels quickly through the fiber by bouncing along the core. The core is surrounded by: Cladding, which is a layer of glass that surrounds the core and contains light pulses to prevent loss Coating, which prevents scratching and other physical damage Buffer, which provides more protection and makes the fiber easier to install Armoring, which protects against damage from crushing, bending and harsh environmental conditions These inner components are enclosed inside a jacket, which protects everything inside. The type of jacket determines which environments the cable can withstand. The cable’s construction allows the fiber to bend and rotate without snapping What’s the difference between singlemode and multimode fiber? Fiber optic cables are categorized into two groups: singlemode and multimode . Each features a different core size to support different transmission distances and bandwidths. Singlemode has a small core that allows a single path (mode) for light to travel through. It’s designed to transmit data across long distances (up to several miles) with little signal loss. These cables are usually yellow in color. Multimode has a larger core that allows multiple light paths (modes) to travel through the cable at the same time. It uses either LEDs or VCSELs (vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers) as light sources. Multimode fiber is ideal for distances of up to a few hundred meters. These cables are usually aqua or erika violet in color. These cables can be joined in one of two ways: Mechanical splicing “holds” the fiber ends together with a special connector Fusion splicing “fuses” or “welds” the fiber ends together using an electric arc What’s the difference between fiber connectors? To connect fiber optic cables, there are several types of fiber connectors to choose from. LC (lucent connector or little connector) connectors are common today, especially in high-density environments like data centers. Because they’re small, cost-effective and easy to install, they are widely used. ST (straight tip) connectors are one of the oldest types of fiber connectors, often found in legacy installations. Made of metal, they’re not suitable for today’s high-density environments, but they are still being used in older systems. SC (subscriber connector or square connector) connectors are slightly larger than LC connectors but are still very popular due to their reliability. MPO (multi-fiber push-on) connectors are newer connectors made for high-density applications, connecting up to 12 fibers through a single plug. VSFF (very small form factor) connectors are ultra-compact connectors that allow for more connections in smaller spaces. How are fiber optic cabling systems managed? In copper systems, components like patch panels are used to organize, protect and manage connections. In fiber systems, connections are managed with cassettes and frames. Frames are centralized hubs that connect and route fiber cables. Connectors can be plugged into the front and back of a frame, and frame options range from simple adapter plates for basic connectivity to more advanced optical distribution frames (ODFs), which are entire cabinets built for high-capacity, high-density environments. Cassettes combine frames and splice trays, housing spliced fibers to maintain proper bend radius and protect connectors. They’re easy to patch in and out. Making the right fiber optic system connections While these questions might seem straightforward, they come up often when discussing fiber optic systems. Having a solid grasp of the basics will help ensure that your network connections are reliable and future-ready. Have questions about fiber optic systems that we didn’t cover in this list? Send us a note; we’ll be happy to answer them! Get answers to your fiber questions. title: Best AI Transcription Software: Top 6 Tools Tested in July 2026
summary: We tested AI transcription software in July 2026. Compare real-time transcription, speaker ID quality, and integration depth across 6 top platforms.
body_text: We tested 6 AI transcription tools in June 2026 because the category has split. Some tools transcribe and stop. Others extract decisions, file tickets, and close the loop before your standup ends. You’re comparing Otter AI sign up flows, best ai transcription software free reddit threads, free automatic transcription software downloads, audio transcription software installs, transcription software free download links for PC, best ai transcription free for PC and best ai transcription app for iphone picks. The real question isn’t transcription accuracy anymore (most tools clear 90% under clean conditions). It’s what happens after the transcript lands. Does it surface action items? Does it route them into Jira or Linear? Or does it hand you a 12-page document and leave the manual work on your plate? This breakdown covers transcription quality, speaker ID under real conditions, integration depth, free tiers that actually work. TLDR: AI transcription tools convert audio to text, but the gap between transcript and action matters most Tools ranked on accuracy across noisy conditions, speaker ID quality, and integration depth with Jira/Slack Otter offers 300 free minutes monthly but stops at transcripts with no ticket creation Spinach files Jira tickets with owners during the call, closing the loop before the meeting ends Spinach fits engineering teams running 4+ weekly ceremonies where manual re-entry accumulates fast What Is AI Transcription Software? AI transcription software uses speech recognition and AI models to automatically convert spoken audio into written text. Feed it a recording, or let it join a live call, and it produces a transcript in seconds without requiring someone to type out every word by hand. The category has grown well beyond raw transcription. Early tools produced walls of text and called it done. Newer tools extract decisions, surface action items, assign owners, and generate summaries from the same audio. AI transcription accuracy benchmark on clean audio, per AssemblyAI’s benchmark, but the gap between “here’s what was said” and “here’s what happens next” is where the most meaningful differentiation between tools actually lives, especially when only 39% of employees receive post-meeting action items despite 54% wanting them, according to Zoom’s meeting statistics research . How We Ranked AI Transcription Software Assessing AI transcription tools requires more than running a few test recordings. Each tool below was assessed against a consistent set of criteria so the rankings reflect real-world performance instead of feature marketing. Here is what drove the scores: Transcription accuracy across audio conditions, including noisy environments, heavy accents, and multi-speaker calls where voices overlap Real-time vs. async processing, since live transcription and file-upload workflows serve fundamentally different use cases Speaker identification quality, because a transcript that labels every line as “Speaker 1” adds manual cleanup time Integration depth with tools like Zoom, Google Meet, Slack, and Jira Free tier and trial availability, since access without a credit card matters for teams testing before committing Pricing transparency across tiers, including where caps and paywalls kick in Best Overall AI Transcription Software: Spinach AI Spinach AI sits at the top of this list not because it transcribes meetings, but because it closes the loop that every other tool on this list leaves open. Transcription is the input. Decisions, action items, and filed tickets are the output. Spinach joins your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams call in real time, captures what gets decided, and surfaces assigned action items before the call ends. A Scrum Master running four ceremonies a week stops spending 10 to 15 minutes after each one re-keying notes into Jira or Linear. That overhead disappears during the meeting, not after the transcript lands. Where tools like Otter or Fireflies hand you a text file and stop, Spinach routes outputs directly into your project management stack. Jira, Linear, Asana, ClickUp, and Notion are all supported. The ticket gets filed with context, an owner, and a due date, far beyond a quote pulled from a transcript. What Spinach Does That Transcription Tools Skip Most AI transcription tools are accurate at capturing words. Spinach is accurate at capturing what those words mean for your sprint. Real-time meeting facilitation: Spinach runs agenda items, tracks time, and flags blockers during the meeting, not after someone reads a transcript. Automatic ticket creation: Action items from standups, planning sessions, and retros become Jira or Linear tickets with owners assigned, filed before the call ends. Decision capture: Spinach logs what was decided instead of what was said, so there is a searchable record of outcomes without the 40-minute wall of text. Native integrations: Slack, Jira, Linear, Asana, ClickUp, Notion, Google Calendar, and Outlook are all supported without middleware. Who Should Use Spinach Engineering leads and Scrum Masters running daily standups, sprint planning, and retros with five or more attendees get the most out of Spinach. The real-time ticket-filing removes the manual re-entry that accumulates across every ceremony. Solo users uploading the occasional recording will find the outcomes layer less relevant than teams with a recurring Agile cadence. Otter Otter is one of the most recognized names in AI transcription, with over 25 million users. It offers real-time transcription, speaker identification, and meeting summaries across Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams. The free tier gives you 300 transcription minutes per month, which covers occasional use but hits limits fast for daily standups or back-to-back interviews. Paid plans start at $16.99/month and add features like custom vocabulary and longer recording limits. Where Otter stops: it delivers a transcript. There are no action items filed, no tickets created, no outcomes tracked. For students capturing lectures or individuals transcribing interviews, that’s enough. For agile teams running ceremonies daily, the transcript is just the beginning of the work. Fireflies.ai Fireflies.ai is a solid choice for teams that need quick, searchable transcripts without much setup. It records meetings across Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams, then produces a transcript with speaker labels, a summary, and a searchable archive your whole team can access. Where it stops short is the handoff. Fireflies gives you the record of what was said, but filing tickets, assigning owners, and updating your backlog still falls on you. For engineering teams running four or five ceremonies a week, that manual step accumulates fast. Who should use Fireflies Teams that primarily need a searchable conversation archive and don’t require real-time ticket creation. If your workflow already has a dedicated person handling post-meeting task triage, Fireflies fits cleanly. If your Scrum Master is also expected to run retros, manage the backlog, and close the loop on action items before the next standup , the gap becomes friction every single day. Fathom Fathom records, transcribes, and summarizes video calls with a focus on keeping the experience lightweight and free. Its free tier is genuinely generous, covering unlimited recordings and transcripts for individuals, which makes it a frequent recommendation in “best free transcription” threads on Reddit. Where Fathom stops: the output is a meeting summary and transcript. There is no ticket creation, no sprint context, and no path from “action item discussed” to “task filed in Jira.” For a solo user capturing client calls or interviews, that is fine. For an engineering team running standups and planning sessions, the gap between transcript and ticket is where time gets lost. Fathom fits teams that want clean, free call recordings with readable summaries. It does not fit teams that need the meeting to produce work; a record alone won’t close the loop. Tactiq Tactiq records and transcribes meetings directly in your browser, requiring no desktop app download. It works as a Chrome extension for Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams, making it one of the lower-friction setups in this roundup. What Tactiq Does Well Real-time captions appear during the meeting, so you can follow along even with noisy audio or accented speakers. Transcripts are timestamped and speaker-labeled, and you can mark key moments mid-call for faster review afterward. The free tier includes unlimited transcriptions, which stands out compared to tools that cap free usage at a few hours per month. Where Tactiq Stops Short Tactiq generates summaries and lets you extract action items post-meeting, but the output is manual. You get a transcript and a text block; what happens next is on you. There is no native ticket creation, no Jira or Linear integration, and no real-time decision capture that feeds directly into your workflow. For a solo researcher or student capturing interview notes, that workflow is fine. For an engineering team running four ceremonies a week, re-keying action items from a text summary into Jira after every call adds up fast. Spinach joins the same meetings and closes that loop before the call ends, turning decisions into assigned tickets without the manual handoff. Jamie Jamie is an AI meeting assistant built for individual contributors instead of teams, with a strong focus on private, local-first note-taking. Unlike most transcription tools that process audio on remote servers, Jamie runs processing on-device by default, which appeals to users with strict data privacy requirements. The core output is a structured meeting summary instead of a raw transcript, which suits users who want decisions and key points without wading through a full verbatim record. Jamie supports over 20 languages and works across any meeting setup without requiring a bot to join the call. Where Jamie falls short is in team collaboration and integrations. There is no real-time ticket creation, no native Jira or Linear sync, and no shared workspace for cross-functional teams. It works well for a solo operator or consultant who attends many calls and needs fast, private summaries, but scales poorly once a team needs shared context and task tracking from those meetings. How do I choose the best AI transcription software for my team? Start with what happens after the transcript. If you need searchable records and readable summaries, tools like Otter or Fireflies work. If you run agile ceremonies and need decisions turned into filed tickets with owners before the call ends, Spinach closes that loop where transcript-only tools stop. Which AI transcription tool works best for daily standups and sprint planning? Spinach is purpose-built for agile ceremonies—it extracts action items, assigns owners, and files tickets in Jira or Linear during the meeting. Tools like Otter and Fireflies produce accurate transcripts but leave you re-keying every action item by hand after the call. Can I use free AI transcription software for a full engineering team? Most free tiers (Otter, Fireflies, Tactiq) support one user or cap monthly minutes at 300–600, which runs out fast across daily standups. Spinach’s free tier covers up to 50 users with full functionality, no minute caps, and no export restrictions. What’s the difference between real-time and file-upload transcription tools? Real-time tools like Spinach, Otter, and Fireflies join live calls and process audio during the meeting, producing outputs before the call ends. File-upload tools (or tools that support both modes) require you to record first, then wait for async processing—fine for solo interviews, limiting for teams that need immediate action-item handoff. When should I pay for a transcription tool instead of using the free tier? Spinach’s paid tier starts around $4/user/month; Otter Pro runs $8.33/user/month with a 1,200-minute cap; Fireflies Pro is $10/user/month. Can I use free transcription software for meetings with technical jargon and acronyms? Free tiers handle clean audio well but accuracy drops when technical terms appear. Otter free caps at 300 minutes monthly and historically mangles jargon like “Kubernetes” into “Cooper Netties,” requiring post-call cleanup. Most free tools stop at transcription and leave you re-typing every action item into Jira afterward. What’s the difference between AI transcription software that joins live calls versus file upload tools? Live-join tools process audio during the meeting and can surface decisions before the call ends, while file-upload tools require you to record first then wait for async processing. For agile teams running daily standups, the live path removes the manual handoff that file-based workflows force on you after every ceremony. Otter AI vs Fireflies for engineering standups? Both transcribe accurately under clean conditions, but neither files tickets or assigns owners. Otter caps free users at 300 minutes monthly; Fireflies locks exports behind paid tiers. Spinach runs the same standup and closes the loop by filing Jira tickets with context before you leave the room. Best AI transcription software free for teams running multiple daily meetings? Spinach’s free tier supports up to 50 users with no minute restrictions and includes ticket creation, where tools like Otter and Tactiq stop at transcripts and force manual follow-up. How accurate is AI transcription software with accents and background noise? Accuracy under noisy conditions varies widely. Most tools clear 90% accuracy with clean studio audio but drop when five engineers talk over each other or heavy accents appear. Speaker identification quality matters as much as raw transcription, since a transcript labeled “Speaker 1” for every line adds manual cleanup time. Can AI transcription software automatically create Jira tickets from meeting decisions? Transcription-only tools like Otter and Fathom produce text but require manual re-entry into Jira. Spinach extracts decisions during the call and files tickets with owners and context before the meeting ends, removing the 10–15 minutes of post-meeting work that accumulates across multiple ceremonies each week. Best free audio transcription software with no download or signup required? Free tiers with genuinely unlimited transcription are rare—Tactiq offers unlimited browser-based captions but still leaves you manually converting summaries into tickets afterward. AI transcription software for students versus engineering teams—what’s different? Students capturing lectures need accurate transcripts and searchable archives, which free tiers from Otter or Fathom handle well. Engineering teams running sprint ceremonies need decisions turned into assigned tasks in real time, not just a document to review later—that’s where transcription-only tools leave a manual gap. Which AI transcription tool integrates natively with Slack and Microsoft Teams for delivery? Spinach delivers summaries and action items directly in Slack and Teams channels, so outputs land in the flow of work without app-switching. Most transcription tools require you to open a separate dashboard to review results, then manually share findings back to your team’s comms platform. Live AI transcription versus post-call transcript processing—which matters for agile workflows? Live transcription processes audio during the call and can route outputs into your workflow before the standup ends. Post-call processing hands you a completed transcript afterward but adds latency and manual steps. For teams running four ceremonies a week, the live path removes the re-keying overhead that async tools force on you every single day. title: Airbnb.org provides free emergency housing after Texas floods
summary: To support communities affected by flooding in Central and South Texas, Airbnb.org, a nonprofit founded by Airbnb to provide emergency housing in times of crisis, is working with nonprofit partners to offer free emergency housing to displaced residents and first responders.
body_text: To support communities affected by flooding in Central and South Texas, Airbnb.org , a nonprofit founded by Airbnb to provide emergency housing in times of crisis, is working with nonprofit partners to offer free emergency housing to displaced residents and first responders. Airbnb.org is partnering with Catholic Charities, Archdiocese of San Antonio to connect displaced residents with free temporary housing. Meanwhile, Airbnb.org is also working with All Hands & Hearts and Operation Blessing to provide housing for their first responders supporting relief efforts. “A comfortable place to call home can help people recover after a disaster, while providing first responders an opportunity to unwind and recharge for the next day,” said Christoph Gorder, Executive Director of Airbnb.org. “We were there for Texas after last summer’s tragic flooding. Working with many of the same partners, including Catholic Charities and All Hands & Hearts, we’re committed to helping the region recover from this latest round of severe weather.” “Our hearts go out to everyone affected by this devastating flooding. We are committed to providing immediate and ongoing support to help our communities recover,” said Ada Saenz, CEO/President of Catholic Charities, Archdiocese of San Antonio. “But we cannot do this alone. The generosity and involvement of our community members play a crucial role in our relief efforts. Every donation makes a meaningful difference in helping families rebuild their lives.” “All Hands & Hearts is proud to stand alongside Airbnb.org in supporting communities affected by the Texas floods,” said Alix Seyfarth, Director of Strategy, All Hands & Hearts. “Right now, our teams are on the ground in Kerr County, and Airbnb’s emergency housing support is providing displaced families and responders a safe place to stay as recovery efforts continue. This partnership reflects the kind of coordinated, community-first response disaster survivors need.” “We’re deeply grateful to Airbnb.org for partnering with Operation Blessing as we respond to disasters, including in Texas. By providing housing for our disaster relief teams, Airbnb.org enables us to focus on what matters most—serving families as they begin the long road to recovery,” said Drew Friedrich, President of Operation Blessing. How it works Airbnb.org partners with local organizations before disaster strikes, so housing support is available quickly. Catholic Charities, Archdiocese of San Antonio is identifying residents in need of temporary housing and referring them to Airbnb.org, which provides credits to book a nearby Airbnb stay that meets their needs—often close to their workplaces, schools, or support networks. Stays are free for guests and are funded by Airbnb.org and the generosity of donors. Residents impacted by flooding in Central and South Texas can request temporary housing support by contacting Catholic Charities, Archdiocese of San Antonio: Region 1 – Texas Hill Country: 210-718-5837 . Counties: Kerr, Kendall, Bandera, Real, Edwards Region 2 – Highway 90 Corridor: 210-935-5885 . Counties: Medina, Uvalde, Frio Region 3 – San Antonio Area: 210-305-6010 . Counties: Bexar, Comal, Atascosa, Wilson, Guadalupe, Gonzales, Karnes Region 4 – Del Rio and Brackettville: 210-278-8381 . Counties: Val Verde, Edwards, Kinney How to help Anyone interested in supporting those impacted by the flooding in Central and South Texas can help by donating to Airbnb.org. 100 percent of donations go directly toward connecting people in crisis with emergency housing. So far this year, Airbnb.org has provided nearly 7,000 nights of free emergency housing in Texas, including after the wildfires in the Texas Panhandle this spring.

title: What Do We Know About Who Watches Major League Baseball on TV and Streaming?
summary: 162 games. Nightly reach. Fans with real spending power. Here's what the viewership data says about who watches MLB on TV and streaming.
body_text: Major League Baseball is massive. Everybody knows it, and the numbers prove it. The 2024 World Series drew an average of 15.81 million viewers across platforms, the most-watched Fall Classic since 2017. The 2025 regular season posted year-over-year viewership gains across every national broadcast partner. MLB.TV recorded 14.5 billion minutes watched in 2024 , then topped it again in 2025 with streaming numbers up 34% from the prior year . Scale is not a question here. But scale is just the opening pitch. The more interesting part of the MLB audience story is about who’s doing the watching now, and the answer has shifted more in the last three years than it did in the previous fifteen. The Audience Everyone Already Suspects Is There MLB’s core viewership is broad, loyal, and heavily invested. The sport draws the second-largest total audience of any professional league in the U.S., trailing only the NFL, and its 162-game regular season means that presence isn’t seasonal, but a nightly drumbeat from April through October. A January 2024 SBRnet survey found that the largest single age segment among MLB attendees and viewers was 50-64, which tracks with a generation that grew up watching games as a social ritual, passed it down, and never really stopped. For advertisers, the profile that follows — established careers, dual-income households, strong brand loyalty, discretionary spending on entertainment and lifestyle — is straightforwardly valuable. According to The Shelf’s analysis of professional sports fan demographics , MLB fans across the five major leagues are consistently described as middle-class men and women with meaningful disposable income across multiple spending categories. The Part of the Audience That Surprises Most Marketers Here’s where the conventional wisdom starts getting complicated. For years, MLB carried a reputation as a sport with an aging problem. The average age of a fan was trending up, and younger audiences seemed to be drifting away. That reputation is starting to change, thanks in part to the pitch clock era, which began in 2023, and compressed games to under two hours and forty minutes on average, the shortest since the mid-1980s. Shorter games increase accessibility, and when combined with a new generation of genuinely marketable stars, younger audiences have become more inclined to take themselves out to the ballgame from the comfort of their own couch. According to MLB , the median age of a ticket buyer has dropped from 51 to 45 since 2019 — a six-year shift in under five years. On the streaming side, the movement is clearer still: the average age of an MLB.TV subscriber dropped from 48 to 44 over the same period. Viewership in the 18-34 demographic grew 12% on ESPN, 24% on FS1, and 9% on Fox during the 2024 season. The network-level growth in this demo was broad enough that Barrett Media noted a 13% gain in 18-34 viewers for the MLB Network Showcase Game series alone in 2025. What’s driving younger fans toward streaming specifically? Partly platform access — younger fans, particularly those aged 18-34, are more than twice as likely to stream live sports compared to older demographics, according to Viant Technology. And MLB has deliberately expanded its streaming footprint to meet them there. As of 2025, 26 of the league’s 30 teams offer standalone DTC streaming options for local fans. The infrastructure is there; the audience is showing up. For advertisers, the 18-34 streaming fan is worth separating from the broader “MLB audience” label. This viewer is paying for access, often out-of-market, actively following a specific team across a long season. That level of intent signals a different kind of attention than someone who happens to catch a game occasionally on cable. The Audience Most Brands Are Underestimating According to ACR viewership data from LG Ad Solutions , female viewership of MLB has seen consistent growth. Because of the stereotype that typical sports fans are male, that finding tends to catch people off-guard, but it aligns with something The Shelf’s analysis found: baseball fans are often described as the most family-oriented fan group among the five major American professional sports leagues. The family dimension of MLB viewership changes how advertisers should think about the audience. A game that runs two and a half hours on a weeknight, in a sport with nearly daily games over six months, tends to pull households into shared viewing in ways that shorter or less frequent sports don’t. It’s background viewing that becomes active viewing when someone hits a grand slam. It’s also a format that holds up across generations in the same room, where a grandparent, a parent, and a teenager can all plausibly have an opinion on who is at-bat. Fifty-seven percent of MLB fans report that they like to stream live sports , according to LG Ad Solutions’ 2022 ACR data, a figure that tracks with the broader directional shift toward streaming across all live sports. That distribution matters: an MLB audience that spans broadcast, CTV, and mobile isn’t consolidated in one place, which means brands that show up across platforms have a better shot at reaching the full household than those anchored to a single linear buy. The female viewer and the co-viewing household don’t always show up in the top-line MLB audience conversation. They should. Both represent reach beyond the assumed sports-fan demographic, and both are watching games in the same high-attention context as the core audience. What This Means for Advertisers Major League Baseball offers a live sports placement without the congestion of the NFL window, across a season that runs nightly from April through the World Series. The audience story above points to a mix of loyal older viewers, a younger streaming cohort that’s actively growing, and a household audience with more breadth than the conventional male sports demo would suggest. For brands in categories like financial services, auto, consumer electronics, retail, food and beverage, or travel, the sustained attention and multi-demographic reach of a full-season MLB buy creates the kind of repeat exposure that builds familiarity, recall, and consideration over time, not just around one event in October.
